chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from some of our companions from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who hastens his zakat before its due time, and he said: 'If eight months have passed, there is no harm.'

And no one should say that these narrations, despite their apparent contradiction, cannot be reconciled, because it is possible to reconcile them. This is because, in our view, advancing zakat is only permissible in the manner of a loan, and the owner of the wealth remains liable for it until the time of zakat arrives and the giver has become wealthy (possessed of nisab). If he has not yet become wealthy, it still suffices for him. And if the advancement is in this manner, there is no difference between advancing by one month, two months, or more than that. And that which indicates this entire principle is what has been narrated:

key_terms.جِهَةِ الْقَرْضِ: In the manner of a loan

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay zakat before the full lunar year has passed?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction in hadiths regarding early zakat payment by establishing the principle of *qard* (loan), where the payer remains liable until the actual due date. This jurisprudential nuance allows for flexibility in timing—whether one month or eight months early—provided the recipient is wealthy enough to repay or the payment serves as a valid discharge. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the conditional nature of zakat obligations and the continuity of liability until the specific *mahill* (due time) arrives.
